title: Spontaneous fission of 238U in LZ's detector components: multiplicity, veto probability and the odds of a lone 248 keV recoil
question: What 238U activity and spontaneous-fission rate do LZ's PTFE, Ti cryostat, PMTs and cables imply (radioassay recall vs (alpha,n)-budget back-calculation vs multiple-scatter cap), and per fission what is the probability that exactly one neutron makes a clean 200-270 keV FV single scatter while the other neutrons, all ~6.5 prompt gammas and the fragments leave no Skin/OD/TPC prompt or delayed-capture signal, giving the expected number of such events in 220 d versus P013's 9e-11?
headline_result: 28 (10-63) fissions per run from a component-resolved 238U inventory, but the silent-companion requirement leaves 1.5e-9 (4e-11 to 1.5e-8) expected lone 200-270 keV single scatters: 16x P013's 9e-11, eight orders short of one event; per-gamma silence is 0.0036 at the PTFE wall vs 0.13-0.15 at the cryostat/PMTs
key_numbers: SF branching 5.45e-7; nu_bar 2.01; f(E_n>8.19 MeV)=5.2e-3 -> 0.29 threshold-capable SF neutrons/run; 238U 2.66 Bq (0.95-6.1) -> 27.6 SF (Ti 11.4, PMTs 12.9, cables 3.1, PTFE 0.10); route B <=2.0 SF, route C <=8.7; p_gamma silent wall 0.0036 / cryostat 0.134 / PMTs 0.148; f_gamma 5e-5 / 2.7e-3 / 3.1e-3; f_n 0.156; P_lone per SF 1.4e-12 to 6.3e-11; total 1.5e-9; effective silent factor 4.6e-4 (P013 3.8e-4); stacked 4e-11 to 1.5e-8; signature 13 TPC deposits, 8.6 MS, 9.8 double-capture fissions per run
model_or_mechanism: 238U spontaneous fission in detector materials; Terrell P(nu), Watt spectrum, prompt-gamma transport MC by source location, P013 neutron transport factors, three inventory normalisations
stance: neutral (tool, projection, or constraint) - spontaneous fission excluded as origin
